newsitem.title: GERMANY: Strong Bunds seen with potential for further gains.
newsitem.headline: Strong Bunds seen with potential for further gains.

text.p: German Bund futures have the potential to keep pushing into higher territory next week after having spent most of Friday clinging to opening levels.
Traders saw no let-up in doubts about European monetary union, which have driven de-convergence trades in Bund's favour, and the market still has needed liquidity to climb.
"In the short-term there appears to be sufficient money and technical factors to drive this market higher," one bond market analyst said.
Late in the afternoon on Friday, the DTB September Bund futures contract was up four basis points at 101.90.

Although Bunds have the potential to climb next week, traders said much was depend on the U.S. debt market. The direction of Treasuries next week looks especially difficult to predict with a FOMC meeting and U.S. jobs data scheduled.
And while Bunds have shown surprising technical strength, they have had a hard time breaking through psychological resistance at 102.00 points.
Much of the de-convergence trend was started by comments from French officials that Paris will not be able to meet Maastricht Treaty deficit criteria in 1997.
But German officials also caused worries about EMU.

Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Friday it would be almost impossible for Germany to meet Maastricht's public debt goal and the stability pact was at risk from less stability-minded nations.
Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber also added to the market uncertainty, saying the Maastricht criteria had to be strictly fulfilled for the euro to be a credible currency.
Next week will see a heavy calendar of Bundesbank speeches and a Bundesbank press conference on Tuesday on Bonn's 30-year bond.
Although some might believe the 30-year bond issue shows Bonn believes the interest rate cycle is at bottom, a bad sign for Bunds, analysts said this issue should cause little concern.
"There is no clear sign that rates are headed higher," one bond market analyst said.
The 10-year cash Bund was up slightly to 102.46 from 102.40 on Thursday to yield 5.66 percent.
